Rashi on Niddah 64b:10:1.english: That she snores - [The Gemara] explains [this] later.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:10:2.english: That the saliva is present - That she sees [blood] due to intercourse.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:13:1.english: "Until the conclusion of Shabbat" we learned - Both during the day and at night.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:14:1.english: That it is permitted to engage in intercourse on Shabbat - Even though he has not yet engaged in intercourse other than two times, and the opening is tight.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:16:1.english: And he engaged in intercourse again - Within the four nights.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:16:2.english: She is ritually impure - For it is menstrual blood.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:18:1.hebrew: בוגרת נותנין לה לילה הראשון - ואפי' לב"ה דאמרי בהגיע זמנה לראות ארבעה, הני מילי נערה, דמשיגיעו ימי הנעורים הוי זמנה; אבל בוגרת — לילה הראשון ותו לא:
Rashi on Niddah 64b:18:1.english: A grown woman is given the first night - And even according to Beit Hillel, who say [that when] her time to see [blood] has arrived, [she is given] four [nights], this applies only to a maiden [na'arah], for once the days of adolescence arrive, that is [considered] her time [to see blood]; but a grown woman [bogeret] [is given only] the first night and no more.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:19:1.hebrew: מתוך שנים עשר חדש - שבעל לילה הראשון, והלך בדרך מיד, ושהה שלשה חדשים, וחזר ובעל ומצא דם, וכן פעם שניה ושלישית, ובא לפני רבי, ואמר: דם בתולים הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 64b:19:1.english: Within twelve months - That he had intercourse on the first night, and immediately went on a journey, and stayed for three months, and returned and had intercourse and found blood; and likewise a second and third time. And he came before Rabbi, and [Rabbi] said: "It is hymeneal blood."

Rashi on Niddah 64b:1:1.hebrew: ונאסר יום עשרים - הבא, שהרי למודה בעשרים ולא עקרתו אלא שני פעמים. שהרי עקירה האחרונה של עשרים האחרונה שלא ראתה, שאחר השלשים שניים, לאו עקירה היא, שהרי לא שינתה ליום שלשים השלישיים, ולא ראתה עד יום עשרים לחדש כווסתה:
Rashi on Niddah 64b:1:1.english: And the twentieth day is prohibited - The upcoming [twentieth day], for she was accustomed to [seeing blood on] the twentieth, and she uprooted it only twice. For the last uprooting of the last twentieth [day] on which she did not see [blood], which was after the second thirtieth [day], is not an uprooting, as she did not change to the third thirtieth [day], and she did not see [blood] until the twentieth day of the month, according to her fixed period.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:1:2.hebrew: מפני שאורח - זה שחזר לשוב יום עשרים, בזמנו הראשון בא:
Rashi on Niddah 64b:1:2.english: Because the menstrual flow - This [flow] that returned to recur on the twentieth day came at its original time.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:2:1.english: Every vine has wine in it - Every woman has virginity and blood.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:2:2.hebrew: ושאין לה הרי זה דור קטוע - וכיון שאין להן דמים מרובים, אין בניהן מרובין:
Rashi on Niddah 64b:2:2.english: And [one] that has none, this is a truncated generation - And since they do not have abundant blood, their children are not numerous.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:5:1.hebrew: תינוקת נותנין לה ארבע לילות - לשמש, ואפי' רואה, אמרינן: דם בתולים הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 64b:5:1.english: A young girl, they give her four nights - To engage in marital relations; and even if she sees [blood], we say that it is hymeneal blood.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:5:2.english: Until the wound heals - [This is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:6:1.english: Her time to see arrived - And she had not seen [blood].

Rashi on Niddah 64b:6:2.english: Until the conclusion of Shabbat - And she was married on Wednesday.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:8:1.hebrew: אפילו ראתה - בבית אביה, אמרו ב"ה: הואיל ולא הגיע זמנה לראות, נותנין לה עד שתחיה המכה:
Rashi on Niddah 64b:8:1.english: Even if she saw - [Blood while still] in her father's house, Beit Hillel say: Since her time to see [menstrual blood] has not arrived, they give her [all blood as pure] until the wound heals.

Rashi on Niddah 64b:8:2.hebrew: מדפליג בסיפא - בהגיע זמנה, קתני חילוק בין ראתה ללא ראתה:
Rashi on Niddah 64b:8:2.english: From the fact that he distinguishes in the latter clause - In [the case of a girl whose] time had arrived [to menstruate], [the mishna] teaches a distinction between [whether] she saw [blood] and [whether] she did not see [blood].

Tosafot on Niddah 64b:10:1.hebrew: כל זמן שהרוק מצוי בתוך הפה - שרואה מחמת תשמיש, תלינן כל היום המחרת וכל הלילה שאחריו, אפילו לא שמשה בהם, בדם בתולים, ואפי' אינה נוחרת; אבל תו לא תלינן, הואיל ולא שמשה, כדאמר לעיל בספ"ק (נדה דף יא:): עבר עליה לילה אחת בלא תשמיש, טמאה. ורב מחמיר טפי, דדוקא כשנוחרת ביום שלאחר תשמיש, תלינן בו ובלילה שלאחריו; אבל בלא נחירה, לא:
Tosafot on Niddah 64b:10:1.english: As long as the saliva is present inside the mouth - [Meaning] that she sees [blood] on account of intercourse: we attribute [the blood throughout] the entire following day and the entire night following it, even if she did not engage in intercourse during them, to hymeneal blood, and even if she is not nohoret; but beyond this we do not attribute [it], since she did not engage in intercourse, as [the Gemara] said above at the end of the first chapter (Niddah 11b): "[If] one night passed for her without intercourse, she is [rendered] ritually impure." And Rav is more stringent, for [in his view] specifically when she is nohoret on the day following intercourse do we attribute [the blood seen] on it and on the night following it, but without nehirah, no.

Tosafot on Niddah 64b:11:1.hebrew: על גבי כולם ורואה על גבי כולם ואינה רואה בידוע שחיתה המכה - לספרים דגרסינן הכי על גבי כלים ורואה, ליכא לפרושי בידוע דאיכא הוכחה, דהא לא מוכח ולא מידי הואיל ורואה; אלא ה"פ: בידוע שיש לתלות שחיתה המכה. וכן צריך לומר בפ' דם הנדה לעיל (נדה דף נו:): בידוע שלפני הכבוס, כלומר שיש לתלותו לפני הכבוס:
Tosafot on Niddah 64b:11:1.english: [If she sits] upon all of them and sees, [or] upon all of them and does not see, it is known that the wound has healed - According to the texts in which we read this, "[if she sits] upon articles (kelim) and sees [blood]," it cannot be explained [that] "it is known" [means] that there is [definitive] proof, for nothing at all is proven, since she sees [blood]. Rather, this is its explanation: "It is known" [means] that one must attribute [the matter to the fact] that the wound has healed. And so one must also say in the chapter "Dam HaNiddah" above (Niddah 56b): "It is known that [it was] before the laundering" — that is to say, that one must attribute it to before the laundering.

Tosafot on Niddah 64b:13:1.hebrew: רב אמר לא הפסידה לילות עד מוצאי שבת תנן - וא"ת: בפ"ק דכתובות (דף ו:) דפריך למאן דאסר לבעול בשבת מדקאמר הכא "עד מוצאי שבת", וקאמר: מאי לאו דאי לא בעיל מצי בעיל? ומשני: לא, כשבעל. ופריך: אי כשבעל, מאי למימרא? ומשני: הא קמ"ל כדשמואל דאמר פרצה דחוקה כו'. והשתא, מאי פריך "מאי למימרא"? הא אשמעינן טובא: דלא הפסידה לילות, כדקאמר הכא! וי"ל, דהתם איכא לישנא דשמואל אוסר למבעל לכתחלה, וכן לרב; ואיצטריך ליה לשנויי הכי לשמואל, דאפילו אי כלוי סבירא ליה דהפסידה לילות:
Tosafot on Niddah 64b:13:1.english: Rav said: She has not lost nights; "until the conclusion of Shabbat" we learned [in the Mishnah] - And if you say: In the first chapter of Ketubot (folio 6b), where [the Gemara] challenges the one who forbids engaging in intercourse on Shabbat from the fact that it says here [in our Mishnah], "until the conclusion of Shabbat," and it says: "What, is it not [referring to a case where] if he did not [yet] engage in intercourse, he may engage in intercourse [even on Shabbat]?" And [the Gemara] answers: "No, [it is referring to a case] where he [already] engaged in intercourse [before Shabbat]." And it challenges: "If [it is referring to a case] where he [already] engaged in intercourse, what is [the Mishnah] coming to tell us?" And it answers: "This teaches us in accordance with Shmuel, who said: [It is permitted to enter into] a narrow opening [on Shabbat], etc." And now, why did [the Gemara] challenge, "What is [the Mishnah] coming to tell us?" Behold, it teaches us a great deal: that she has not lost nights, as [Rav] says here! And one can say that there [in Ketubot], there is a version [according to which] Shmuel forbids engaging in intercourse ab initio, and likewise [a version according to which] Rav [forbids it]; and it was necessary for [the Gemara] to answer this way for Shmuel, since even if he holds like Levi that she has lost nights [the Mishnah is still needed to teach his ruling of a narrow opening].

Tosafot on Niddah 64b:14:1.hebrew: דשרי למבעל לכתחלה כדשמואל כו' - אף על גב דבפ"ק דכתובות (דף ו:) מייתי הך דשמואל אבעילה שניה, מ"מ לפי האמת דשרי למבעל בתחלה, נקט הכא, דהוי רבותא טפי:
Tosafot on Niddah 64b:14:1.english: That it is permitted to engage in intercourse for the first time [on Shabbat], in accordance with [the opinion of] Shmuel, etc. - Although in the first chapter of Ketubot (6b), [the Gemara] brings this [statement] of Shmuel with regard to a second act of intercourse, nevertheless, according to the truth [of the matter] that it is permitted to engage in intercourse for the first time [on Shabbat], [the Gemara] cited [it] here, as that is a greater novelty.

Tosafot on Niddah 64b:16:1.hebrew: רבי אסי אמר טהורה - ואף על גב דלית ליה הך סברא דאם איתא דהוה דם מעיקרא הוה אתי, מיהו ס"ל שפיר הא דרב גידל דלעיל ספ"ק (דף יא:), דאם פסקה מחמת תשמיש וראתה, אפילו מחמת תשמיש, טמאה. דאם איתא דדם בתולין הוא, מעיקרא כששמשה הוה אתי ולא הוה לה למפסק מחמת תשמיש; כיון דבתחלה בעל ומצא דם, אם איתא שנשאר עוד דם בתולין, לא היה לה לפסוק כששמשה. אבל הכא איירי דבעל ולא מצא דם, ולהכי איכא למימר דבעל כדשמואל:
Tosafot on Niddah 64b:16:1.english: Rabbi Asi says: She is pure - And even though he does not accept this reasoning that if it were [virginity] blood it would have come at the outset, nevertheless he certainly holds of that [statement] of Rav Giddal above at the end of the first chapter (daf 11b), that if she ceased [bleeding] as a result of intercourse and [subsequently] saw [blood], even as a result of intercourse, she is impure. For if it were virginity blood, it would have come earlier when she engaged in intercourse, and she would not have ceased [bleeding] as a result of intercourse; since initially he engaged in intercourse and found blood, if it were so that more virginity blood remained, she would not have ceased [bleeding] when she engaged in intercourse. But here, we are dealing with [a case where] he engaged in intercourse and did not find blood, and therefore it can be said that he engaged in intercourse like Shmuel.

Tosafot on Niddah 64b:17:1.hebrew: שאני שמואל דרב גובריה - משמע הכא דשמואל לא שכיחא. וכן בפרק קמא דחגיגה (דף יד:) גבי בתולה שעיברה — פירוש: שהושיבוה על פי החבית ואין ריחה נודף, ובזה נודע שהיא בתולה — ומפיק דכשרה לכהן גדול, דאיכא למימר באמבטי עיברה, דשכיח טפי מדשמואל. וקשה, דבפרק קמא דכתובות (דף ו:) קאמר: רוב בקיאין בהטיה! ויש לומר, דהטיה דכתובות אינה בעילה גמורה שתתעבר בה כבשאר ביאות:
Tosafot on Niddah 64b:17:1.english: Shmuel is different, as his strength was great - It is implied here that [an occurrence like] that of Shmuel is not common. And so too in the first chapter of Chagigah (daf 14b) regarding a virgin who became pregnant — meaning, that they seated her on the opening of a [wine] barrel and its scent did not emanate [from her mouth], and through this it was known that she was a virgin — and it concludes that she is fit for a High Priest, for it can be said that she became pregnant in a bathtub, which is more common than [an occurrence like] that of Shmuel. And [this is] difficult, for in the first chapter of Ketubot (daf 6b), it says: The majority are skilled in slantwise intercourse (hataya)! And one can say that the slantwise intercourse of Ketubot is not a complete act of intercourse such that she could become pregnant through it as in other acts of intercourse.

Tosafot on Niddah 64b:6:1.hebrew: ד' לילות - ב"ה לא בעו רצופין, כדאמר בגמרא: מעשה ונתן לה רבי ד' לילות מתוך שנים עשר חדש. וכן נראה, דד' לילות לב"ש אפילו מפוזרות, כמו לב"ה:
Tosafot on Niddah 64b:6:1.english: Four nights - Beit Hillel do not require [the nights to be] consecutive, as it says in the Gemara: "There was an incident, and Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] gave her four nights within twelve months." And similarly, it appears that the four nights according to Beit Shammai are [granted] even [if they are] spread out, just as according to Beit Hillel.
